mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES stays near its current depressed level or falls further, weekday trip chains into shopping districts remain suppressed and RETAIL_REC stays below its prior four-week mean over the next month.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES is still about -15% from baseline at t-0w and has not recovered above t-2w levels
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its last-4-weeks mean for most of the next four weeks while WORKPLACES remains near or below -15%.

mechanism_narrative: A further decline in TRANSIT below its recent trough reduces spontaneous shopping trips and late-week retail visits within one week, pushing RETAIL_REC down relative to the past four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT has hovered around -28% to -30% across the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline within the next week after TRANSIT crosses below -30%, or RETAIL_REC improves despite continued transit weakness.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM and RESIDENTIAL both rise while WORKPLACES stays weak, households consolidate errands near home and substitute away from discretionary retail, lowering RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL remains above baseline while WORKPLACES remains well below baseline
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next two weeks even though GROCERY_PHARM and RESIDENTIAL are elevated and WORKPLACES stays depressed.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in PARKS after a recent trough acts as a short-lag proxy for improved weather and outdoor activity, which pulls more people into surrounding retail areas and lifts RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS turns up by at least 5 points from its recent weekly low
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from -5.3 at t-3w to -22.1 at t-1w, then partially recovered to -16.9 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains below its last-4-weeks mean over the next month after PARKS rebounds by at least 5 points from the recent low.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both remain suppressed, policy constraints on movement continue to limit discretionary shopping trips, keeping RETAIL_REC below the prior four-week average over the next month.
evidence_refs: fact:Both series are materially below baseline throughout the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC improves over the next four weeks while TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both stay near their current depressed levels.

mechanism_narrative: A near-baseline or rising GROCERY_PHARM series indicates errand bundling and routine shopping stability; this supports discretionary store visits and nudges RETAIL_REC upward within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises to above -4% and holds there for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM is consistently close to baseline, between -4.7 and -3.3 in the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise within two weeks after GROCERY_PHARM moves above -4% for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL usage is elevated while TRANSIT stays weak, people substitute home-based activity for out-of-home shopping, causing RETAIL_REC to stay below its last-month average over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL remains above +7% while TRANSIT remains below -25%
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL is above baseline and TRANSIT is far below baseline in every week of the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its previous four-week mean even though RESIDENTIAL stays above +7% and TRANSIT stays below -25%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained stabilization in PARKS together with mild improvement in WORKPLACES signals broader mobility normalization, which should translate into a modest retail rebound after a four-week lag.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rebounded from -22.1 at t-1w to -16.9 at t-0w while WORKPLACES is flat at -15.1
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to outperform its prior four-week mean over the next month despite PARKS stabilizing and WORKPLACES improving from its recent trough.
